brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Evening edition. It covers the 24 hours to 17:10 CET on 29 October; new research covers 05:10 CET to 17:10 CET on 29 October, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Russian Jet Drone Kills 14 on a Crowded Platform at Ukraine's Dnipro Station
items.lede: Six of the wounded, among them an 11-year-old boy, are in serious condition, and Zelensky used the attack to demand fresh Western sanctions on Moscow.

sections.text: A Russian jet-powered drone hit a platform at the railway station in Dnipro, Ukraine, at about 11:00 Kyiv time (10:00 CET) on Thursday 29 October, where train No. 866 to Zaporizhzhia was standing [1][2]. Regional head Oleksandr Hanzha put the toll at 14 dead and 14 injured, six seriously, including an 11-year-old boy [1][3][4]. The Air Force said three of four jet drones aimed at the region were shot down [5][4]. Railway chief Oleksandr Pertsovskyi said many people were on the platform despite an elevated threat alert [2][3]. President Volodymyr Zelensky called for new EU, U.S., and G7 sanctions and said sanctions must not be eased while the war continues [6][4]. The BBC said Russia's military had not commented [3].
Confidence is high on the strike and the toll, because the BBC, DW, and two Ukrainian outlets carry the same on-record figures from regional, railway, and national officials.

items.title: Drone Hits Apartment Block in Ukraine's Kremenchuk, Killing Three
items.lede: Fifteen people were hurt in the Poltava-region city, three of them children, and parked cars burned outside, the regional governor said.

sections.text: A Russian drone struck an apartment building in Kremenchuk in Ukraine's Poltava region on Thursday 29 October, regional governor Vitalii Diakivnych and the State Emergency Service said [7][8]. Diakivnych said parked cars caught fire, that the injured count rose to 15 by 13:36 Kyiv time, and that the death toll rose to three at 13:53 Kyiv time (12:53 CET) [8]. Three children are among the injured [7]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the deaths and injuries, because two Ukrainian outlets carry the same on-record figures from the governor and the emergency service.

items.title: Russia's Defence Ministry Claims 1,214 Ukrainian Drones Shot Down Overnight
items.lede: Kyiv's General Staff claimed hits on drone depots and two radars in Bryansk, while smoke rose over a defence-linked chemical plant in Bashkortostan.

sections.text: Russia's Defence Ministry said on Thursday 29 October that its air defences intercepted 1,214 Ukrainian drones overnight over regions including Bryansk, Belgorod, Kursk, Moscow, Bashkortostan, and Udmurtia [9][10]. Ukraine's General Staff said its forces hit a Geran drone store, a drone launch site, and a fuel depot near Navlya in Russia's Bryansk region, plus two radar stations near Starodub and Medvyodovo [11][12]. Monitoring channels and the outlet Astra reported a drone attack on Sterlitamak in Bashkortostan, with smoke near the Bashkir Soda Company chemical plant, which The Moscow Times said is on Russia's closed register of defence enterprises [13][14]. No Russian official comment on damage was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the ministry made the claim, because Interfax and Reuters report it. Confidence is low on the interception figure and the Ukrainian strike results rest on each side's own claims, and the Sterlitamak damage is unconfirmed.

items.title: Two 15-Year-Old Girls Die as Russia Strikes Central Chernihiv
items.lede: Police counted 23 wounded, including a ten-month-old baby, after shops and cars caught fire in the northern city's centre.

sections.text: A Russian drone struck the centre of Chernihiv in northern Ukraine on Thursday 29 October, setting shops and cars on fire, city military administration head Dmytro Bryzhynskyi and the city council said [15][16]. Regional governor Viacheslav Chaus said two 15-year-old girls were killed [15]. Police said as of 13:30 Kyiv time (12:30 CET) that 23 people were injured, among them a ten-month-old girl, a ten-year-old, and two teenagers aged 16 and 17 [16]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the deaths, because two Ukrainian outlets carry the same on-record account from city and regional officials. The figure of 23 injured rests on police as reported by one outlet; the other gave 11 at an earlier hour.

items.title: Ukraine's Air Force Reports 112 Russian Drones Launched Overnight, 97 Stopped
items.lede: Hits landed at seven sites and ten of the 40 jet-powered Shaheds were not stopped, with the attack still under way on Thursday morning.

sections.text: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 112 drones at Ukraine from 18:00 Kyiv time on 28 October (17:00 CET), Shaheds, 40 of them jet-powered, plus Gerbera attack drones and Parodiya decoys, from the directions of Oryol, Millerovo, and occupied Donetsk [17][18]. It said that as of 08:00 Kyiv time (07:00 CET) on Thursday 97 had been shot down or suppressed, including 30 jet-powered drones [17][18]. Hits were recorded at seven locations and falling debris at five, and about seven drones were still in the air [18].
Confidence is high on the figures, because two Ukrainian outlets carry the same on-record Air Force tally. The figures are the Air Force's own and were not independently checked.

items.title: Ukraine's Rights Commissioner Travels Toward Occupied Oleshky as the Truce Holds
items.lede: Civilians choosing Kyiv-held territory would be flown via Russia and Belarus, likely on Saturday, after aid arrives on Friday, Lubinets's office said.

sections.text: Ukraine and Russia have observed a ceasefire around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in Ukraine's Kherson region, since 03:00 Kyiv time on 27 October (02:00 CET) [19][20]. U.S. First Lady Melania Trump, who brokered the pause, said on Tuesday its area had been widened within the Kherson region [21][22], and lawmaker David Arakhamia said it runs until 22:59 Kyiv time on 1 November [23]. The BBC said an estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people remain in Oleshky [24]. On Thursday Ukraine's human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said the truce had held for 54 hours with no violations, that routes were still being demined, and that aid would be delivered on Friday [25]. Arakhamia said Lubinets had set off for Oleshky at the head of a Ukrainian delegation [26]. Lubinets's office said residents leaving for Ukraine will travel through Russia and Belarus, and Fox News published a document from Russia's ombudsman Yana Lantratova describing flights from Anapa to Gomel, likely on Saturday 31 October [27]. The office said the document was not a military or political agreement [27].

Confidence is high that the pause is holding, because Ukrainian, Russian, and U.S. figures say so on record. The evacuation route through Russia and Belarus rests on Lubinets's office and a document reported by Fox News, read via one Ukrainian outlet.

items.title: Kremlin Aide Ties Timing of Russia-Ukraine-US Talks to the Battlefield
items.lede: Yury Ushakov said the date will come only after 4 November, while Zelensky still expects a meeting in Abu Dhabi by 10 November.

sections.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on 27 October that no date had been set for new trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the United States in Abu Dhabi [28][20]. A Kremlin readout of Putin's call that day with Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said all three welcomed an agreement to resume the talks in early to mid November [29]. On Wednesday Peskov said the date would be announced once fixed [30][31], and presidential aide Yury Ushakov told Vesti the talks are expected around mid-November and that no Europeans would be invited [31][32]. In the Netherlands, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv expects the meeting by 10 November, with energy and sea ceasefires, prisoner exchanges, and humanitarian issues on the agenda [33]. Early on Thursday Ushakov told Interfax the date would be set after 4 November, that timing depends on the situation on the battlefield, and that Russia's delegation would be finalised soon [34]. No U.S. date was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that no date had been fixed by Thursday, because Russian officials said so on record and Zelensky gave only an expectation. The 10 November timing rests on Zelensky alone, and Ushakov's latest remarks on one Ukrainian outlet citing Interfax.

items.title: Russian Munition Kills Two Ukrainian Deminers in the Sumy Region
items.lede: The two men from a rapid-response demining group in Shostka district died after an explosion, one at the scene and one in hospital, rescuers said.

sections.text: Ukraine's State Emergency Service said two of its bomb disposal experts, Oleksandr Kovalchuk, 32, and Denys Sydorych, 39, were killed on 28 October during humanitarian demining in the Shostka district of Sumy region [35][36]. It said a Russian munition detonated while the team was working; one man died at the scene and the other died after being taken to hospital in critical condition [35][36]. Service chief Andrii Danik announced the deaths [36].
Confidence is high on the deaths, because two Ukrainian outlets carry the same on-record account from the emergency service. The cause of the blast rests on that service alone.

items.title: Russian Attacks Wound Six in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk Region, Including a Teenager
items.lede: A 15-year-old in Pavlohrad was among the hurt, and a late strike on a Dnipro factory put a 35-year-old man in hospital.

sections.text: Oleksandr Hanzha, head of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk regional military administration, said Russian forces attacked four districts more than 40 times on Wednesday 28 October with drones, artillery, and aerial bombs, injuring five people [37][38]. A 15-year-old boy was hospitalised in Pavlohrad, two people were hurt in the Nikopol district, and two men, one in serious condition, after strikes on a petrol station in the Synelnykove district [37][38]. On Wednesday evening Russia hit an industrial facility in Dnipro, starting a fire, and Hanzha later said a 35-year-old man there was hospitalised [39][40]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the strikes and injuries, because two Ukrainian outlets carry the same on-record figures from the regional head and the emergency service.

items.title: Wednesday Drone Attack Kills a 60-Year-Old Man in Ukraine's Kharkiv
items.lede: Rescuers later said the drone set a postal warehouse ablaze across 1,000 square metres and raised the injured count to four.

sections.text: A Russian attack drone struck Kharkiv's Osnovianskyi district again on Wednesday 28 October, starting a fire, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said [41][42]. Regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said a 60-year-old man was killed and three men aged 46, 56, and 41 were taken to hospital with injuries of varying severity [43][41][42]. Ukrainska Pravda said a 48-year-old woman also needed medical help [41]. On Wednesday evening Ukraine's State Emergency Service put the toll at one dead and four injured, and said the drone hit a postal warehouse, starting a fire over 1,000 square metres [44]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the death and the injuries, because Ukrainian outlets carry on-record figures from the mayor, the governor, and the emergency service. The warehouse detail and the fire area rest on the emergency service as reported by one outlet.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Belgium's Finance Ministry Pulls Its MyMinfin Tax Portal Offline After a Cyberattack
items.lede: Officials say no taxpayer data leaked, filing deadlines move to 16 November, and federal police are investigating with no group yet named.

sections.text: Belgium's federal Finance Ministry (FOD Financiën) took MyMinfin, Tax-on-web, and Biztax offline after intruders penetrated its systems during the night from Tuesday to Wednesday, spokesman Francis Adyns said [1][2]. The outage was first reported on Wednesday evening [3]. The ministry said it detected the attack within a few hours, saw several attempts to alter parts of its digital environment, and contained the intrusion before attackers could take over applications or reach data [1][2]. It said there were no indications of a data breach and that the services must be rebuilt in an isolated environment, without giving a restoration date [1][2]. Tax returns due on 31 October can now be filed until 16 November [1][2]. Belgium's federal police and the Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium are investigating; no group has been named, and no claim of responsibility was found by the cutoff [1].
Confidence is high on the outage, the containment, and the deadline change, which the ministry stated on record and Belga and The Register carried. No attribution was found.

items.title: Danish Intelligence Warns Ukrainian Refugees Against Russian Sabotage Recruitment
items.lede: PET says Moscow could also aim to discredit refugees, with tasks disguised as journalism or market research and handlers hidden behind intermediaries.

sections.text: Denmark's Security and Intelligence Service (PET) on Thursday morning issued its sabotage-recruitment warning in Ukrainian, saying Russian intelligence services may try to use Ukrainian refugees in Denmark to prepare or carry out sabotage [4][5]. PET said Russia may also want to cast Ukrainian refugees in a bad light by making it look as if they back Russian sabotage [4][5]. Tasks such as photographing a company, checking access routes, or passing on harmless-seeming information can be disguised as journalism, market research, or documentation, and handlers may hide behind intermediaries [4][5]. Counter-espionage chief Emil Græsholm said the earlier warning to Danes now also had to reach Ukrainians [4]. PET says there is concrete Russian planning and preparation of sabotage in Denmark, an assessment Russia's embassy rejected in September [5].

Confidence is high that PET issued the warning and on its wording, which DR and Ritzau relayed from the press release. The PET release itself was not opened, and no new arrest or incident was announced.

items.title: Bulgaria's Military Prosecutors Open a Case as the Drone-Struck Contship Jet Sinks
items.lede: Military prosecutors cite prohibited methods of warfare against a neutral-flagged ship, at least six vessels were attacked off Bulgaria this month, and officials expect no major pollution.

sections.text: Bulgaria's Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov said on Wednesday that three maritime drones struck the Liberian-flagged container ship Contship Jet in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, about 21 miles from Shabla [6][7]. The rescue centre in Constanța received the report at 12:01 Sofia time (11:01 CET), and all 18 crew, 14 Filipinos and four Ukrainians, were rescued and taken to Varna [6][7][8]. The ship later sank, and Bulgaria's Maritime Administration expected no significant harm to the sea or coast [9][10]. Reuters reported the cargo included lithium-ion batteries, corrosive liquids, and acids, and that at least six ships have been attacked off Bulgaria this month [10]. Navy commander Kiril Mihaylov said a French patrol aircraft spotted the drones first and that some containers fell overboard [11]. On Thursday the Sofia Military District Prosecutor's Office opened pre-trial proceedings under Article 415 of the Criminal Code, which covers prohibited methods of warfare, citing the attack on a ship flying the flag of neutral Liberia, and ordered Varna military police to question the crew [12][13].

Confidence is high on the strike, the rescue, the sinking, and the prosecutor's case, which Bulgarian officials stated on record and Reuters carried. No attribution was found, and the earlier conflict over how many drones hit the ship is unresolved.

items.title: Dutch Police Detain a Belgium-Based Man Over Drone Flights Above Eemshaven Port
items.lede: The suspect has gone back to Belgium, police have not said what he is suspected of, and the port handles NATO allies' military cargo.

sections.text: Police in the Netherlands confirmed on Wednesday that they detained a man living in Belgium on Tuesday of last week after several reports of suspicious drone flights over the Eemshaven area, ANP reported [14]. Flying drones over Eemshaven is banned because it is a site of vital infrastructure with a permanent Dutch Defence presence, and much NATO partner equipment is transshipped through the port [14]. The man has returned to Belgium but remains a suspect; a police spokesperson could not say what exactly he is suspected of, and his age and nationality were not released [14]. RTV Noord reported other suspicious drone sightings in Groningen province, including near the Farmsum chemical park, but police see no link and have made no other arrests [14].
Confidence is moderate: the detention rests on a police confirmation carried by ANP in one outlet read. No motive or foreign link was stated by the cutoff.

items.title: Moldova's President Convenes the National Security Council Over a Massive Data Breach
items.lede: Officials say pension, disability, and banking details on about 750,000 people may have been taken, and the e-government agency's head was dismissed.

sections.text: Moldova's Prime Minister Vasile Tofan told Wednesday's government meeting that attacks on public digital services between 19 and 23 October targeted about one million personal identification numbers, with at least one data element extracted in about 750,000 cases [15]. He said the services were investigating possible involvement of foreign state actors [15]. On Wednesday evening President Maia Sandu convened the National Security Council for the coming days, and the presidency said the attack was most likely enabled by artificial intelligence [16][17]. The cybersecurity service STISC said exposed data may include pensions, disability status, driving licences, photographs, and IBAN codes, and that failed new attempts followed on 25 and 27 October [18]. AFP reported that Tofan dismissed the e-government agency's director, Nicoleta Colomeet [17]. No state was named by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the figures, the council meeting, and the dismissal, which Moldova's government, presidency, and cybersecurity service stated on record and AFP carried. Foreign state involvement is under investigation and unconfirmed.

items.title: Poland and Germany Hold Three Suspects in Romania's Russia-Linked Brașov Arson Case
items.lede: Munich prosecutors now confirm the two Belarusians have been jailed since 7 October over a paid arson plot near Nuremberg, while Romania seeks all three extraditions.

sections.text: Romania's Intelligence Service (SRI) said on 26 October that a sabotage network coordinated from Russia set the 14 September fire on the Carfil industrial platform in Brașov, next to a subsidiary of state arms maker Romarm [19][20]. Romania summoned Russia's ambassador on Tuesday over what its Foreign Ministry called a clear act of hybrid warfare [21], and the Russian Embassy rejected the unsubstantiated accusations [22]. Poland's Central Investigation Bureau (CBŚP) said officers detained the Ukrainian suspect in Warsaw on Monday under a Romanian European Arrest Warrant [23][24]. Der Spiegel reported that the two Belarusians, aged 39 and 50, are held in Bavaria [25][26]. Germany's Munich General Prosecutor's Office told Reuters on Wednesday that they have been in custody since 7 October and planned, for payment and for an unnamed foreign government or organization, to set fire to a building or critical infrastructure near Nuremberg [27]. Romanian prosecutors are seeking all three extraditions [27].

Confidence is high on the Warsaw detention and the Bavarian arrests, which Poland's CBŚP and Munich prosecutors confirmed on record. The Russian direction rests on Romanian intelligence and Der Spiegel's sources; German prosecutors did not name a state.

theaters.heading: Politics, security, and defense across the EU and NATO's European members

items.title: ECB President Lagarde Will Step Down in February, Nine Months Early
items.lede: EU leaders have started choosing her successor immediately, and the euro-area bank held its deposit rate at 2.5 per cent the same day.

sections.text: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde told the Governing Council in Frankfurt, Germany, and European Council President António Costa on Thursday that she will leave on 7 February 2027, the ECB said [1]. Franceinfo, citing AFP, put the departure nearly nine months before her term ends [2]. Costa said the process to appoint her successor under Article 283 of the EU treaty began the same day, with a decision by euro-area leaders [3]. At its meeting the same day, the ECB left rates unchanged, with the deposit rate at 2.50 per cent, the main refinancing rate at 2.65 per cent, and the marginal lending rate at 2.90 per cent [4][2]. The bank said financing conditions had tightened since September, after two rate rises this year driven by energy prices [2]. No reason for the early exit was given in the ECB statement.
Confidence is high on the departure date and the rate decision, stated by the ECB and the European Council and reported by ANSA and franceinfo.

items.title: Von der Leyen Keeps Pitching Associate Membership to Canada at Montreal Summit
items.lede: Germany and other EU states had the term struck from the draft statement, while Ottawa says the label matters less than the ties themselves.

sections.text: The European Union has dropped Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's offer of associate membership talks for Canada from the draft statement for the EU–Canada summit in Montreal on Thursday and Friday, El País and the Guardian reported [5][6]. The draft seen by the Guardian instead commits both sides to define by the 2027 summit an ever closer association of Canada to the EU, short of full membership [6]. EU ambassadors raised legal and political concerns on Monday; Italy proposed keeping the Commission's wording, while Germany pushed the softer formula, the Guardian reported [6]. Prime Minister Mark Carney has framed the relationship as a partnership for the future [5]. At the summit on Thursday, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen still described associate membership as a partnership closer to membership than anything the EU has done before, open only to its closest partners outside Europe, the BBC reported [7]. Germany's ambassador to Canada said the term is used for Ukraine and Moldova, and Prime Minister Mark Carney said the nomenclature does not matter [7].

Confidence is high that the wording was dropped from the draft and on von der Leyen's remarks, reported by El País, the Guardian, and the BBC; the member-state positions rest on unnamed diplomatic sourcing.

items.title: France's Interior Minister Warns Prefects of Very High Violence Risk on Saturday
items.lede: Nuñez ordered a heavy police deployment for 31 October, after Macron's call for calm and with the casseurs-payeurs bill and riot surcharge still pending.

sections.text: France's Senate adopted the casseurs-payeurs bill on Wednesday by 229 votes to 105, making everyone in a violent gathering jointly liable for damage [8]. Arrests in the 24 October marches reached 1,314, with 53 officers injured [9][10]. In Reims, the police watchdog IGPN was tasked with investigating after a police grenade seriously injured a marcher's shin, franceinfo reported [11]. Franceinfo reported a planned compulsory 0.8 per cent riot insurance surcharge from 1 January 2027, which the Conseil d'État must still validate [12]. On Wednesday evening President Emmanuel Macron called for calm, conceding the response had been too slow [13]. On Thursday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez wrote to prefects that the risk of urban violence on Saturday is very high, citing online calls to gather in city centres around Halloween, franceinfo reported [14]. He asked for a powerful, reactive, and agile deployment [14]. Yellow Vests called 31 October protests; the Snes-FSU teachers' union plans a 5 November march [10][15]. Labour Minister Jean-Pierre Farandou backed temporary voluntary Sunday opening for shops hit by protests [16].

Confidence is high on the vote, the planned surcharge, the arrests, and the statements, reported on record by Public Sénat and franceinfo; the letter's contents rest on franceinfo's reading of it. No new baton charges were reported by the cutoff.

items.title: Spain's Train Crash Toll Rises to 69 as Drivers Strike Over Rail Safety
items.lede: The Civil Guard says 64 people were reported missing, and the opposition wants an independent review of the network after a second deadly collision this year.

sections.text: Spain's state-run Renfe AVE high-speed train ran into the back of a stationary private Iryo train on the Madrid–Andalusia line in Toledo province at about 08:53 on Wednesday, El País reported [17][18]. Transport Minister Óscar Puente said the LZB signalling system failed at about 08:30, halting six trains, and that the Adif control centre ordered them at about 08:36 to resume normal running, calling the decision inexplicable [17][18]. One more body was found overnight, raising the toll to 69, the Guardian reported on Thursday; the Civil Guard opened DNA offices in Madrid, Toledo, Córdoba, and Seville, and said 64 people had been reported missing [19]. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who declared three days of mourning, said in Toledo that safety measures would be strengthened [20][19]. Train drivers held a previously planned strike for rail safety investment, and opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo demanded an independent review of the whole network [19]. The CSIF union demanded Puente's resignation [21].
Confidence is high on the toll, the mourning, and the official statements, reported by the Guardian, the BBC, and El País; the cause rests on the government's preliminary account.

items.title: Czech Students Call 3 November Strike Over Plan to Scrap Public-Media Fees
items.lede: President Petr Pavel warned on Wednesday against ill-considered changes that break up the media space, as Czech students and broadcast staff prepare a walkout.

sections.text: Thousands filled Prague's Old Town Square in the Czech Republic on Sunday to protest a coalition bill replacing Czech Television and Czech Radio licence fees with state funding, ČTK reported [22][23]. The lower house passed the bill in first reading on Saturday; it would cut their funding by about CZK 1.4 billion [22][23]. On Tuesday evening National Theatre drama unions declared a strike alert, demanding the withdrawal of the funding bill and the resignation of Culture Minister Oto Klempíř [24]. Chamber speaker Tomio Okamura said he would back abolishing Czech Television and Czech Radio if someone proposed it, ČT24 reported [25]. On Monday afternoon Babiš also rejected Czech Radio director René Zavoral's call for a public debate, calling him an 'activist director' who should resign [26]. On Wednesday about 2,000 people protested in Brno, where a student committee called a nationwide strike for 3 November, the day Czech Television and Czech Radio staff plan an all-day strike [27] [23]. At the state honours ceremony on Wednesday evening, President Petr Pavel urged building trust in established media rather than wrecking the media space with ill-considered changes [28].
Confidence is high on the protests, the vote, the strike calls, and the president's remarks, reported by ČTK, ČT24, and Expats.cz; the Brno figure is an official's estimate.

items.title: Spanish Police Arrest Valencia Teenager Accused of Organising Halloween Looting
items.lede: The 17-year-old is linked to Blocus, which has called for disorder in the city centre on Saturday, and goes before juvenile prosecutors on Thursday.

sections.text: Spain's National Police detained a 17-year-old in Valencia on Wednesday morning, accused of using messaging groups to call for looting and riots in the city centre on Saturday 31 October, EFE and Europa Press reported [29][30]. He faces counts of conspiracy to cause public disorder, conspiracy to commit property crimes, and membership of an organised group [29][30]. Police sources linked him to Blocus, the movement that called for Saturday's disorder, and said he would go before the juvenile prosecutor on Thursday [30]. The government delegation had already announced a special security operation for Saturday afternoon [29]. Police said more details would follow on Thursday [29].
Confidence is high on the arrest and charges, reported by EFE and Europa Press from police sources; the Blocus link rests on police sources and Levante-EMV.

items.title: Netherlands Pledges 500 Million Euros for Ukrainian Air Defence During Zelensky Visit
items.lede: The money was already earmarked, and a separate 1.2-billion-euro civilian package over three years was announced in Kyiv the same day.

sections.text: Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten announced a 500-million-euro winter package for Ukraine's air defence and drones after meeting President Volodymyr Zelensky in The Hague on Wednesday, NOS reported [31][32]. The money had already been reserved for Ukraine [31]. Jetten called Dutch support rock solid and urged other European states to keep helping, citing intensified Russian attacks on civilian targets and infrastructure before winter [31][32]. Zelensky said the aid was needed for the winter [32]. In Kyiv, Trade and Development Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma announced 1.2 billion euros of non-military aid over three years, including 40 million euros this year for the Ukraine Energy Support Fund [31].
Confidence is high on the amounts and statements, reported by NOS and RTBF from the press conference and the minister's announcement.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Saeima Lets Latvian Border Guards Fire Without Warning to Repel Attacks
items.lede: Lawmakers framed the amendments as a response to hybrid warfare on the eastern frontier, and any death or injury must reach prosecutors within 24 hours.

sections.text: Latvia's Saeima on Thursday adopted amendments to the State Border Guard Law and the Criminal Procedure Law giving border guards explicit rights to use physical force, combat techniques, weapons, and dogs to repel attacks on people or border infrastructure, LSM reported [1]. A weapon may be used without warning when a warning is not possible [1]. The law previously did not spell out such rights [1]. Defence Committee chair Raimonds Bergmanis said a hybrid war is under way at Latvia's external border [1]. Offences by border guards under the enhanced border regime will be investigated by the State Border Guard's own officials [1]. No statement from the State Border Guard was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the vote rests on one LSM report; the adopted text was not read.

items.title: EU Commission Turns Down Baltic States' €500 Million Anti-Drone Funding Request
items.lede: Defence Commissioner Kubilius points Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia instead to a coming SAFE loan call, where about €21 billion remains unallocated.

sections.text: The European Commission has answered a late-September letter from the defence ministers of Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia seeking €500 million for anti-drone defences, but offered no new funding on that scale, LRT reported on Thursday [2]. Commissioner Andrius Kubilius told LRT on Wednesday that one option is the SAFE loan instrument, with a new call coming soon because €21 billion remained after the first round [2]. He said few other large EU budget sources exist as the budget period nears its end [2]. Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas said the three states wanted to combine drone detection, artificial intelligence, and interception into an integrated air defence system [2]. ELTA, as carried by tv3.lt, separately reported the Commission's answer, and President Gitanas Nausėda said on Thursday that Lithuania will consider SAFE loans while defence purchases stay funded from the state budget [3]. ERR carried LRT's account [4]. No written Commission statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that the request was turned down, reported by LRT and ELTA with Kubilius and Nausėda on record; the Commission's reply letter was not read.

items.title: Zelenskyy Wants to Attend Ukraine Recovery Conference in Estonia, Tsahkna Says
items.lede: Invitations to world leaders for the 28–29 January Tallinn meeting are signed, though the foreign minister says attendance depends on wartime conditions in January.

sections.text: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said at the government's weekly press conference on Thursday that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wants to attend the Ukraine Recovery Conference in Tallinn, ERR reported [5]. He said Zelenskyy and Prime Minister Kristen Michal have signed personal invitations to leaders, and the event will be held at world-leader level [5]. Tsahkna said attendance depends on the situation in Ukraine in January, after media speculation that a hard winter could keep Kyiv's leadership away [5]. He said the aim is billions in additional funding for Ukraine [5]. The conference is set for 28 and 29 January [5]. No Ukrainian presidential office statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the remarks rest on one ERR report of an on-record press conference; Kyiv's side was not read.

items.title: Lithuania Sets 2032 Start for Universal Military Conscription
items.lede: The annual intake would rise from just over 5,000 to about 7,500 young people, after the military asked for time to train instructors and build barracks.

sections.text: Lithuania's State Defence Council agreed on Thursday to introduce universal military conscription in 2032, President Gitanas Nausėda told reporters after the meeting, BNS reported via LRT [6]. Women would still serve only voluntarily [6]. Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius said the government wanted a faster transition but the military said it would be ready by 2032 [6]. Preparations include training about 300 instructors and building housing for draftees [6]. The council also agreed to widen service options, such as drone operator training and support to the border guard and rescue services [6]. Lithuania restored partial conscription in 2015 [6]. No published council decision text was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the decision rests on one BNS report via LRT quoting the president and prime minister on record.

items.title: Lithuania Charges Two Germany-Based Men With Terrorism Over Starlink Arson Attempt
items.lede: The dual nationals in their 20s were already held in Germany at Bulgaria's request, and investigators tie them to similar attacks in Poland and Bulgaria.

sections.text: Lithuanian law enforcement said on Thursday that two men in their 20s suspected of trying to set fire to Starlink equipment in Vilnius earlier this month have been arrested in Germany at Bulgaria's request [7]. One holds German and Turkish citizenship and the other German and Serbian, Saulius Briginas of the Lithuanian Criminal Police Bureau said [7]. He said the men arrived the day before, left right after, and had prepared in advance [7]. Prosecutor Nėrijus Puškorius said they are suspected of terrorist offences; a transfer decision comes later [7]. Reuters, citing the Prosecutor General's Office, reported that both were charged and that Lithuania treats the 18 October attempt as Russia-linked sabotage aimed at Ukraine's military capabilities [8]. Investigators link them to Starlink arson cases in Poland and Bulgaria [7]. The target was premises of Lithuanian firm Delska, where SpaceX stores Starlink gear [7]. Moscow has called such accusations baseless [8]. No German authority statement was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the arrests and charges, reported by BNS via LRT and Reuters from Lithuanian police and prosecutors on record; the Russia link is Lithuania's assessment; no German source was read.

items.title: Lithuania Weighs Palantir Battlefield Software for Its Armed Forces
items.lede: TV3 puts the first seven years of use at nearly €200 million, and Defence Minister Kaunas says planned spending may need shifting to pay for it.

sections.text: Lithuania's Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas told TV3 News on Wednesday that the country is considering buying an artificial intelligence system from US company Palantir for its armed forces, BNS reported via LRT on Thursday [9]. He said the system would integrate large volumes of data and support battlefield decision-making, and that NATO countries need such software [9]. TV3 reported the first seven years would cost nearly €200 million, possibly more [9]. Kaunas said some reallocation of funds may be needed because the final price is not yet known [9]. No Palantir statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the minister's remarks rest on one BNS report via LRT; the cost figure is TV3's and was not read directly.

items.title: Latvia's President Will Ask Kulbergs on 4 November to Form a Government
items.lede: Rinkēvičs says he is confident a cabinet will emerge, while United List is reported to want Edvards Smiltēns as speaker of the new Saeima.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs said on Latvian Radio on Thursday that on the morning of 4 November he will sign an order inviting Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs of the United List to form the next cabinet, giving him legal standing to proceed [10]. Rinkēvičs called the situation not ordinary but said he was confident a government would be formed and that the rest is up to the parties [10]. The newly elected Saeima first meets on 3 November [10]. United List holds 41 seats, enough for a minimal majority with the National Alliance's ten, or a broader one adding New Unity's seven [10]. Kulbergs opened formal coalition talks on Wednesday [11]. Latvian Television reported on Wednesday that United List plans to put Edvards Smiltēns forward as speaker and former president Raimonds Vējonis as a deputy speaker, leaving New Unity without a presidium post [12]. No United List statement confirming the presidium plan was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the nomination date, stated by the president on Latvian Radio; confidence is moderate on the presidium plan, which rests on one LTV report citing unnamed information.

items.title: Estonia's President Was Not Told in Advance of Nordic Leaders' Putin Call, Adviser Says
items.lede: Rainer Saks, the president's new security adviser, calls Europe's lack of a common line on talking to Moscow regrettable but backs steps that bring peace closer.

sections.text: Rainer Saks, newly appointed security adviser to Estonia's President Madise, said on ETV's 'Esimene stuudio' on Wednesday evening that the president was not informed beforehand of the Norwegian prime minister's and Finnish president's Tuesday phone call with Vladimir Putin [13]. He said diplomats briefed the presidential office in Kadriorg after the call [13]. Saks said it was logical that Estonia was not asked for input, since Ukraine had asked Norway and Finland directly and Finland stressed it spoke only for the two countries [13]. He called the call positive if it moves the peace process in a direction favourable to Ukraine and if Kyiv is satisfied [13]. He said it is somewhat regrettable that Europe has no common position on how to deal with Russia, and that Europe is not mature enough to talk with Putin because no joint plan exists [13]. No statement from the president herself was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the remarks rest on one ERR report of a broadcast interview; the president's office was not read directly.

items.title: Latvia Will Keep Secret Its Tests for Stolen Ukrainian Grain in Russian Transit
items.lede: The food safety service sampled Russian cargoes over a month ago, results are still pending, and the public will not learn if any stolen grain is found.

sections.text: Latvia's Food and Veterinary Service (PVD) will not publicly disclose whether Russian grain shipped through Latvia includes grain stolen from Ukraine's occupied territories, Latvian Television found, LSM reported on Wednesday evening [14]. The government gave the PVD powers in September to test grain origin in a laboratory, and the service took samples from Russian transit cargoes more than a month ago [14]. The results have not yet arrived [14]. Last week Agriculture Minister Uldis Augulis signed a memorandum with Ukraine and the United Kingdom on cooperation in grain sampling and laboratory testing methods [14]. No PVD statement explaining the decision was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the decision rests on one LTV report; no PVD document was read.

items.title: North Macedonia Treads Carefully on Bulgaria Dispute During Sofia's Election Race
items.lede: North Macedonia's foreign minister said no meeting with his Bulgarian counterpart is planned before December's NATO and OSCE gatherings, while Slovakia pledged strong support for Skopje's EU bid.

sections.text: North Macedonia's Foreign Minister Timco Mucunski said on Thursday in Skopje that his government was in dialogue with Bulgaria, the EU institutions, and all member states on unblocking its EU accession, but would be cautious so as not to become part of Bulgaria's presidential campaign [1] [2]. He spoke at a joint press conference with visiting Slovak Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar [1]. Mucunski said he could meet Bulgarian Foreign Minister Velislava Petrova on the sidelines of NATO and OSCE meetings in December and sought a long-term agreement rather than a temporary fix [1]. Asked about the escape of Iva Mihailova, he called it unacceptable for Bulgaria to serve as a refuge for people convicted or facing legal proceedings, Albeu reported [2]. He said he had recently presented Skopje's position to France's minister for European affairs in Montenegro [1]. Blanar said North Macedonia could count on Slovakia's strong support [1]. No Bulgarian government response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the press-conference remarks, reported by BTA and Albeu; the refuge remark appears only in Albeu.

items.title: Serbian Public Broadcaster's Chief Quits Under Pressure From Student List
items.lede: RTS's governing board meets Friday to name an acting head after Manja Grcic reversed, within a day, her refusal to step down.

sections.text: Manja Grcic, director-general of Serbia's public broadcaster RTS, resigned on Wednesday evening, a day after ruling out stepping down, BIRN's Balkan Insight reported on Thursday [3]. The Student List, which won an absolute majority in Sunday's election, had demanded in an open letter on Tuesday that RTS management and news editors resign, accusing them of political bias [3]. Grcic said she knew some viewers saw her staying "even temporarily" as an obstacle to change [3]. Before leaving she dismissed news editor-in-chief Bojana Mladjenovic [3]. Board president Branislav Klanscek told FoNet the board would meet on Friday and denied reports that deputy Dejan Jovanovic had already been named [3]. Student List candidate Nemanja Karovic said the movement does not want to control RTS, only to see it follow the law [3]. On Monday the provincial broadcaster RTV apologised on air for years of one-sided reporting [3]. No acting director-general had been named by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the resignation and board plans rest on one BIRN report citing FoNet; the resignation time is given only as Wednesday evening.

items.title: Kosovo Suspends Peja's Top Prosecutors and 11 Police Officers Over Femicide
items.lede: The move follows BIRN's finding that Arlinda Zekaj told police her brother-in-law, now accused of the axe killing, had threatened her life three days earlier.

sections.text: Kosovo's Prosecutorial Council on Thursday suspended Peja chief prosecutor Lumturije Vucetaj and her deputy Arlinda Nallbani Gacaferri, who coordinated domestic-violence cases, council member Dardan Vuniqi told BIRN [4]. Kosovo Police suspended 11 officers in the Peja region at the Police Inspectorate's request, including the regional director, a station commander, and the head of investigations [4]. Zekaj was killed on Sunday evening in Vitomirica near Peja after police accompanied her home, and a judge had let her and her ex-husband keep sharing a house two metres apart [5]. Her brother-in-law Albert Sylaj was remanded for 30 days on Wednesday on suspicion of the killing; her ex-husband Jeton Sylaj was remanded on Tuesday for violating a court order [4]. Hundreds marched in Pristina on Wednesday demanding that Justice Minister Donika Gervalla and Interior Minister Xhelal Svecla resign [5]. Prime Minister Albin Kurti blamed the judiciary at a government meeting on Wednesday [5]. Activists said protests would continue on Thursday [4]. No ministerial response to the resignation calls was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the suspensions, remands, and protests rest on BIRN reporting alone, though it quotes a named council member.

items.title: Bulgaria's Yotova and Gyurov Agree to One Live TV Debate Before the Run-Off
items.lede: Public broadcaster BNT hosts the only head-to-head on Thursday evening, after Gyurov accused the government of using official channels to campaign for the acting president.

sections.text: Bulgaria's Central Election Commission had acting President Iliana Yotova on 34.76 percent and former caretaker premier Andrey Gyurov on 31.95 percent, BNT reported [6]. With no majority won, the commission on Tuesday set a 1 November run-off [7] [6]. On Monday Prime Minister Rumen Radev cast Gyurov's pro-EU, pro-Ukraine stance as warmongering [8]. Government channels urged a vote for Yotova, which Gyurov said breached the electoral code [9]. On Wednesday evening the election commission found, by 8 votes to 7, that Radev had committed no administrative violation, and referred the complaints about official channels to the National Audit Office; the Yes, Bulgaria party, part of Democratic Bulgaria, said it would appeal immediately [10] [11]. On Thursday, Gyurov's nomination committee appealed the ruling to the Supreme Administrative Court and filed a new complaint that the call to vote for Yotova was still on the government's website after the run-off campaign began, asking for a ruling within the 24-hour legal deadline [12]. The two meet in the campaign's only televised debate on BNT on 29 October at 20:00 CET, moderated by Poli Zlatareva [13] [14].
Confidence is high on the results, run-off date, and debate, reported by BNT, BTA, The Sofia Globe, and Novinite; the commission ruling comes from BTA and Dnes.bg.

items.title: Serbia's Election Winners Promise a Lawful Handover While Vučić Allies Hold Power
items.lede: The Student List's anti-corruption plan must wait at least a month for mandates to be verified, leaving police, prosecutors, and most media under the outgoing camp.

sections.text: Serbia's Student List, which is set to hold around 140 of the National Assembly's 250 seats after the 25 October election, says it will take power only through legal procedure, The Christian Science Monitor reported on Wednesday [15]. Until the new parliament and government are constituted, Aleksandar Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party keeps caretaker control of the security services, army, prosecutors, and police, and acting president Ana Brnabić is a close Vučić ally [15]. The new majority will not be verified for at least another month, and most media remain under the influence of Vučić and his allies [15]. The bloc's "Student Plan" puts anti-corruption first, including confiscating illegally acquired wealth, a special prosecutorial police force, and vetting officials [15]. Political scientist Dušan Spasojević warned that Progressive Party obstruction could leave the bloc with a majority it cannot use [15]. Top candidate Ilija Srdanović told Croatian and Montenegrin media on Tuesday that the bloc's values are close to European ones and he sees no obstacle to EU integration [15]. No Student List leadership vote result was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one Christian Science Monitor report with named sources; the seat count is preliminary.

items.title: Albanian Journalists' Union Logs 51 Attacks on Media During Tirana Protests
items.lede: The association blames police for 41 of the incidents and wants answers from the national police chief, as Wednesday's 16th protest day dwindled to a small group.

sections.text: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama on Sunday announced a package against "violence and urban anarchy" after weeks of clashes in Tirana, blaming opposition leader Sali Berisha, "Antifa extremists", and foreign actors [16]. RTSH reported on Monday that in 13 days of protests police had arrested more than 270 people, prosecuted 344, and suspended nine officers for excessive force [17]. The Health Ministry said on 19 October that 310 people had been injured since the protests began, including 191 police officers, Albanian Daily News reported [18]. On Wednesday, the 16th day, CNA reported a low turnout of students and lecturers outside the Education Ministry; Rama, whose invitations to dialogue students have repeatedly rejected, again ruled out resigning [19]. By Wednesday afternoon only a small group remained outside the Prime Minister's Office, CNA reported [20]. On Wednesday evening the Journalists' Association of Albania said it had documented 51 attacks on journalists and media workers since 13 October, 41 of them by police, and six in which journalists or media workers were hit by rubber bullets; it asked State Police chief Skënder Hita to explain [21]. No police response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: arrest and injury figures are official, while Wednesday's turnout and the journalists' tally rest on CNA alone.

items.title: Armenia's Deputy Speaker Hurls Chair as Parliament Brawl Leaves MPs Hurt
items.lede: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan condemned violence yet called his party's response proportionate, while the human rights ombudsman demanded a legal investigation.

sections.text: A brawl broke out in Armenia's parliament on Thursday between MPs of the ruling Civil Contract party and the opposition Strong Armenia faction, OC Media reported [1]. It began when Civil Contract MP Taron Chakhoyan accused the opposition of corruption and mocked Strong Armenia leader Narek Karapetyan's family [1]. Deputy Speaker Vahagn Aleksanyan threw a chair towards opposition MPs, bottles were thrown, and MPs left with injuries and torn clothing; Speaker Ruben Rubinyan called a recess of about an hour [1]. Citing RFE/RL, OC Media said the fight continued in the corridors until security staff separated the sides [1]. Rubinyan blamed Karapetyan for starting it, and Pashinyan said "whether with a chair or something else, it is proportionate and right" [1]. Karapetyan called it "a normal Armenian-style man-to-man fight" [1]. Ombudsman Anahit Manasyan said the incident must be investigated under the law [1]. No count of injured MPs was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on OC Media, which drew on the official livestream and RFE/RL; no second outlet was read.

items.title: Moscow Forum Launches Foundation to Restore Georgia–Russia Diplomatic Ties
items.lede: Its co-founders include fugitive former prosecutor general Otar Partskhaladze, who is sanctioned by the US and UK and wanted by Georgian authorities.

sections.text: A forum in Moscow on Wednesday proposed a Russian-Georgian university, wider teaching of Russian in Georgia, and restored services at Lomisi Church as steps towards renewing diplomatic relations, which Georgia and Russia cut after the 2008 war, OC Media reported on Thursday [2]. Participants set up a foundation called Unity of Russians and Georgians, co-founded by Partskhaladze, Moscow-based businessman Mamuka Pipia of the pro-Russian Solidarity for Peace party, and Davit Tsetskhladze of the Russian-Georgian Business Council [2]. Russian Foreign Ministry official Vasily Gavrilov attended and said better relations served both countries [2]. The Russian Interests Section at the Swiss Embassy in Tbilisi said the event aimed to promote restored relations and called on President Vladimir Putin and Georgia's government to back closer ties [2]. The forum came a week after Georgia named First Deputy Foreign Minister Giorgi Zurabashvili the prime minister's special representative for relations with Russia [2]. No Georgian government comment on the forum was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one OC Media report drawing partly on Sputnik Georgia footage; no second outlet was read.

items.title: Pashinyan Says Armenia May Avoid Snap Elections Over a New Constitution
items.lede: Justice Minister Srbuhi Galyan said a draft charter will be ready in mid-November, and Pashinyan hopes to make a referendum offer the opposition cannot refuse, though he gave no guarantee.

sections.text: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan told a press briefing on Thursday there was a high probability that the matter would not reach snap parliamentary elections [3]. He had earlier floated early elections to win the constitutional majority his Civil Contract party needs for constitutional change, which Azerbaijan demands as a precondition for a peace deal [4]. Pashinyan said Wednesday's government question session in parliament made it possible to build strong public pressure on the opposition to allow, with its votes, a referendum on a new constitution, though he could not guarantee he would be able to formulate that proposal [3]. Justice Minister Srbuhi Galyan told Factor.am the draft would be ready in mid-November and discussed at length, and called snap elections "one of the very good options" that had not been decided [5]. Galyan told reporters the government's agenda was to write a new constitution, not to remove anything from the current one, when asked about Baku's demand to drop the reference to Armenia's Declaration of Independence [6]. No response from the Strong Armenia opposition faction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: Pashinyan's and Galyan's remarks rest on NEWS.am reports, one relayed from Factor.am; OC Media supplies only the background.

items.title: Georgian Opposition Turns Party-Ban Test Against Georgian Dream in Court
items.lede: Council of Europe chief Alain Berset warned that a ban needs a strong legal basis and could reach the Strasbourg court, with hearings scheduled to run to 30 October.

sections.text: Georgia's Constitutional Court began substantive hearings on Monday on a lawsuit by 88 Georgian Dream MPs to declare five opposition parties unconstitutional: Unity – National Movement, Coalition for Change, Lelo – Strong Georgia, Gakharia for Georgia, and the Federalists [7]. The suit accuses them of seeking to overthrow the constitutional order; all five deny it [7]. The court refused to call Bidzina Ivanishvili and other ruling-party figures as witnesses [7] [8]. On the sixth day, Court President Revaz Nadaraia twice cut off coalition lawyers, ruling a European Parliament resolution irrelevant and calling coalition lawyer Giga Lemonjava's argument that the suit echoes Russia's account of the 2008 war "demagoguery" [9]. Hearings are scheduled to continue through 30 October, and a ruling is due by 24 June 2027 [9]. On Thursday coalition lawyer Nika Gvaramia argued that, by the lawsuit's own standard, Georgian Dream itself should be banned [10]. Council of Europe Secretary General Alain Berset said in Strasbourg on 27 October that a ban needs a strong legal basis and the case could reach the European Court of Human Rights, JAMnews reported on Thursday [11].
Confidence is high on the court's earlier rulings, reported by JAMnews and The Messenger; Thursday's remarks by Gvaramia and Berset each rest on one outlet.

items.title: Baden-Württemberg Interior Minister Hagel Warns Stone-Throwers Ahead of Saturday Youth Rallies
items.lede: Germany's national pupils' body has distanced itself from the movement over its murky organisation and plans a separate Berlin protest on 20 November.

sections.text: Rallies by the 'Gen Z regelt' or 'Gen Z steht auf' initiative are planned in about 30 German cities on Saturday, and security authorities are preparing, tagesschau reported [1]. Baden-Württemberg Interior Minister Manuel Hagel (CDU) told the Mannheimer Morgen that peaceful protesters are protected by the Basic Law and the police, but whoever throws stones loses both [2]. He defended his earlier 'violent mob' remark, which the state's Left party said disparaged the protests, saying it meant those planning to bring violence from the neighbouring country, where he said 2,400 people were arrested in a single day and 150 police officers injured [2]. The initiative rejects violence; its website's legal notice changed twice in a week and on Thursday showed a Swiss address [2] [1]. The Federal Students' Conference distanced itself, citing the group's unclear structure, and plans its own protest in Berlin on 20 November [1].

Confidence is high on the planned rallies and Hagel's remarks, reported by tagesschau and by the Stuttgarter Zeitung via dpa. The arrest and injury figures are Hagel's own and were not checked against French official data in this run.

items.title: Berlin's New State Parliament Elects Hendrikje Klein as Its First Left Party President
items.lede: Germany's far-right AfD failed to win a vice-presidency in the same secret ballots, leaving one of the two deputy posts vacant for now.

sections.text: The Berlin House of Representatives, the state parliament of Germany's capital, held its constituent session about six weeks after the 20 September election and elected Left Party politician Hendrikje Klein, 46, as president with 98 of 149 votes, 42 against, and nine abstentions [3] [4] [5]. She is the first Left politician in the post and the third woman; the Left, as the largest group, had the right to nominate [3] [5]. AfD candidate Martin Trefzer won only 40 of 149 votes for vice-president, while CDU candidate and former president Cornelia Seibeld was elected with 109; the AfD vote was adjourned, leaving one of the two deputy posts vacant for now [4] [3] [5]. The chamber has 153 seats, 45 of them held by the Left [3].
Confidence is high on the vote figures, stated in the parliament's own notice and reported by tagesschau and rbb24.

items.title: Germany's Health Minister Won't Rule Out Cuts to Long-Term Care Benefits
items.lede: The number of Germans needing care has risen from two million to more than six million in 20 years, he said, while patient advocates warned families would buckle.

sections.text: Germany's federal health minister Carsten Linnemann (CDU) told the Handelsblatt that long-term care insurance must save around ten per cent and he could not guarantee there would be no benefit cuts [6]. Without reform, the scheme faced a deficit of about eight billion euros in 2027, he said; he rejected compulsory private top-up insurance and criticised the SPD's call to cap residents' own payments in care homes [6]. Eugen Brysch of the German Foundation for Patient Protection said cuts would push the roughly five million people cared for at home, and their relatives, to the brink of collapse [6]. A 13-member government care commission began work this week and is due to make proposals by the end of January [6].
Confidence is high that Linnemann made the remarks, reported by tagesschau from his Handelsblatt interview; no second outlet was read by the cutoff.

items.title: German Prosecutors Say Belarusian Suspects Carried Fuel Canisters to Nuremberg–Würzburg Line
items.lede: Romania also wants both men extradited over a September fire in Brașov, but Bavaria's prosecutors say their own case takes priority.

sections.text: Munich's general prosecutor's office in Germany said on Thursday that two Belarusian men, aged 39 and 50, were caught beside the main Nuremberg–Würzburg rail line at Langenfeld, in Bavaria, with four canisters of highly flammable material [7]. Alexander Ecker, head of Bavaria's extremism and terrorism unit ZET, said they were seen depositing the canisters and were handling them directly at the power and rail line; a power pylon stood nearby, and the exact target is still under investigation [7]. Whether a foreign government or organisation commissioned them is also still under investigation, Ecker said [7]. The men have been in pre-trial custody since 7 October; Der Spiegel first reported the case [8] [9]. Romania, which links them to a 14 September fire at an industrial building next to a state arms firm in Brașov, seeks their extradition, but Ecker said the German case comes first [7] [10]. No Belarusian or Russian statement was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the arrest site, the canisters, and the custody, stated on record by the Munich general prosecutor's office and reported by BR24 and tagesschau. Confidence is moderate on the intended target and any sponsor, which prosecutors say are still under investigation.

items.title: IG Metall Rejects Employers' First Offer for Germany's 3.7 Million Metalworkers
items.lede: Warning strikes can begin Sunday when the peace obligation ends, after talks failed in Bavaria, Lower Saxony, Baden-Württemberg, Hesse-Rhineland-Palatinate-Saarland, Thuringia, and, on Thursday, Berlin-Brandenburg and Saxony-Anhalt.

sections.text: IG Metall on Tuesday rejected employers' first offer for just over 3.7 million German metal and electrical workers: a one-off 1 percent of annual pay in July 2027 and a 1.3 percent rise in July 2028 [11] [12]. On Wednesday, Mitte region talks in Hanau for about 388,000 workers in Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate, and Saarland failed; district head Jörg Köhlinger called the offer "lousy" and said warning strikes would start at 00:01 on Sunday, 1 November [13] [14]. Talks in Eisenach for about 28,000 Thuringian workers failed that evening; Köhlinger called strikes unavoidable [15]. On Thursday, second-round talks in Berlin for about 96,000 workers in Berlin and Brandenburg also failed; district head Jan Otto said the offer amounted to a sharp real-terms pay cut and was 'not negotiable', and that warning strikes from 1 November were being prepared, while employers' negotiator Henning Brandes said intensive strikes would be 'absolutely the wrong signal' [16]. Talks in Magdeburg for Saxony-Anhalt ended without result the same day, with no third round scheduled; district head Thorsten Gröger called the offer 'too low, too late' and said warning strikes would start from 1 November [17].
Confidence is high on the offer, rejection, and strike timetable, from tagesschau, dpa, and IG Metall.

items.title: Gen Z Activists Blockade Universities in Berlin, Leipzig, and Hamburg
items.lede: Germany's federal interior ministry sees no concrete calls to violence before Saturday's nationwide youth rallies, which activists link to the protests in France.

sections.text: Protesters from the 'Gen Z regelt' initiative on Wednesday barricaded entrances of the Free University's Otto-Suhr-Institut in Berlin, Germany, with fences and bins; the university moved teaching online [18] [19]. Social media posts showed similar blockades at the main campus of Leipzig University and at Hamburg's HAW Finkenau campus [19]. The activists oppose cuts to universities, rearmament, and military conscription, and called for nationwide protests on 31 October; one told dpa that the protests from France were reaching Germany [18] [19]. Police said no criminal complaint was filed in Berlin [18]. A federal interior ministry spokesman said federal security agencies had no further evidence of concrete calls to violence or planned riots [19].

Confidence is high on the Berlin blockade, reported by rbb24 and the Stuttgarter Zeitung. Confidence is moderate on Leipzig and Hamburg, which rest on social media posts cited by the Stuttgarter Zeitung.
